_about: Public-domain Alexander Carson (1776-1844), Irish Baptist minister of Tubbermore, for the Word Hoard: Reasons for Separating from the General Synod of Ulster (1805), A Reply to Mr. Brown's Vindication of the Presbyterian Form of Church Government (1807), History of Providence as manifested in Scripture (1840), Baptism in its Mode and Subjects (1845), The Romish Controversy (1852) and The Inspiration of the Scriptures (1853), from Internet Archive scans. Added 2026-10-23 by lane A, round 49 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

carson-reasons-for-separating: Reasons for Separating from the General Synod of Ulster (1805)
carson-reply-to-brown: A reply to Mr. Brown's vindication of the Presbyterian form of church-government : in which the order of the apostolical churches is defended. In a series of letters to the author (Edinburgh : J. Ritchie, 1807)
carson-history-of-providence: History of providence, as manifested in scripture : or, Facts from scripture illustrative of the government of God (Edinburgh : William Whyte, 1840)
carson-baptism: Baptism in its mode and subjects (Philadelphia : American Baptist Publication Society, 1845)
carson-romish-controversy: The Romish controversy; being a series of essays and letters on some of the leading doctrines of the church of Rome. To which is added, a sermon on the encouragements to the propagation of the Gospel, preached at Surrey Chapel, London (New York, Hanna & Carson, 1852)
carson-inspiration: The inspiration of the Scriptures : a review of the theories of the Reverend Daniel Wilson, Reverend Dr. Pye Smith, and the Reverend Dr. Dick, and other treaties (New York : Edward H. Fletcher, 1853)

_alternates.carson-copies: Other printings of Baptism in its Mode and Subjects (1831-1860), the 1852 History of Providence and Providence Unfolded (1851)

_excluded.carson-other: The 1805 Mode and Subjects of Baptism examined (Daniel Merrill's book); Independent or Democratic Church Government (1868, another author)
